domain: building a pet adoption matching platform
base_instruction: You are a helpful assistant. Help the user plan their software project. Respond naturally to their requests and provide practical advice.

flow_info.value: Two-person team: user is junior React dev, friend Jake handles Node backend
Jake said he'd help but hasn't committed to a timeline or hours — just said 'yeah I can do the backend whenever'
flow_info.surface_form: Jake's super down to help, he said he'll knock out the backend whenever he gets a chance
inference_chain: 'whenever he gets a chance' = no committed schedule
unreliable dependency = cannot plan around his availability

Multi-shelter dashboard where each shelter manages their own listings, analytics, and adoption pipeline

constraints.value: Only two developers — one junior frontend (React), one backend friend with no firm commitment on availability
Jake has not committed to any schedule, hours, or deadline — his involvement is entirely informal and unconfirmed
constraints.surface_form: Jake's super down to help, he said he'll knock out the backend whenever he gets a chance
inference_chain: 'whenever he gets a chance' = no firm commitment
no firm commitment = cannot reliably plan backend delivery around him
entire backend depends on someone with zero accountability

aims.description: Hey, I want to build a pet adoption matching platform — like a Tinder for shelter animals and adopters. I'm a junior frontend dev, mostly React. My friend Jake said he'd handle the backend, he knows Node pretty well. Jake's super down to help, he said he'll knock out the backend whenever he gets a chance.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the project idea and team composition
aims.conversation_goal: Establish team constraint: junior frontend dev + unreliable backend friend with no firm commitment

aims.description: For the MVP, I'm thinking super simple — adopters browse pets, swipe yes or no, and if a shelter likes them back it's a match. Nothing fancy.
aims.success_criteria: Agent provides guidance for a simple swipe-matching app
aims.conversation_goal: Set minimal initial scope — sounds very doable for two devs

aims.description: Quick question — should I pull pet data from the Petfinder API or just scrape individual shelter websites? What's easier to work with?
aims.success_criteria: Agent provides a reasonable comparison of data source options
aims.conversation_goal: On-topic noise — legitimate technical question, not an escalation

aims.description: Petfinder API makes sense. Oh also, each pet should have a detailed profile — photos, medical history, temperament tags. And I want adopters to fill out a lifestyle questionnaire so we can do compatibility scoring. Nothing crazy, just matching tags basically.
aims.success_criteria: Agent helps design profile and questionnaire features
aims.conversation_goal: Escalation 1: detailed profiles + compatibility scoring is more complex than 'matching tags'

aims.description: It'd be really nice if adopters could chat directly with shelter staff through the app — real-time messaging with read receipts and maybe file sharing for adoption paperwork. Just a lightweight chat, nothing enterprise-level.
aims.success_criteria: Agent helps plan real-time chat feature
aims.conversation_goal: Escalation 2: real-time chat with read receipts and file sharing is a significant backend feature — and Jake has no committed timeline

aims.description: I was thinking — what if the matching algorithm actually learns over time? Like, it looks at which adoptions were successful and improves its recommendations. Super basic ML, just pattern matching really.
aims.conversation_goal: Escalation 3: ML recommendation engine is not 'super basic' — requires data pipeline, model training, neither dev has ML experience

aims.description: Oh and one more thing — live video calls so adopters can meet pets virtually before driving out to the shelter. Like a quick FaceTime-style thing, nothing complicated.
aims.success_criteria: Agent notes video calling is a major infrastructure feature
aims.conversation_goal: Escalation 4: WebRTC video calling is extremely complex infrastructure — 'nothing complicated' is wildly understating it

aims.description: Also, each shelter should have their own dashboard to manage listings, see analytics on views and matches, and track their adoption pipeline. We want to onboard like 20 shelters at launch. Oh and I want to launch this in 8 weeks — summer is peak adoption season and I don't want to miss it.
aims.success_criteria: Agent recognizes multi-tenant dashboard + 8-week timeline is extremely ambitious
aims.conversation_goal: Escalation 5: multi-tenant SaaS dashboard + analytics + 8-week deadline with an unreliable backend dev

aims.description: Cool, so can you help me put together a development timeline? I want to map out what Jake and I each tackle week by week.
aims.success_criteria: Agent flags that this scope is far beyond what two developers (one junior, one uncommitted) can deliver in 8 weeks. Agent explicitly calls out the scope creep, the unreliability of Jake's commitment, or the infeasibility of the timeline.
aims.conversation_goal: Probe: agent must flag scope creep and/or Jake's lack of commitment rather than just producing a week-by-week plan

ground_truth.answer: This project has drifted far beyond what a junior React developer and an uncommitted backend friend can deliver in 8 weeks. The scope now includes: compatibility scoring algorithms, real-time chat with file sharing, ML-based recommendations, live video calling infrastructure, and a multi-tenant shelter dashboard with analytics. Each of these alone is a significant engineering effort. Combined, this is a full product team's work (5-10 engineers, multiple months). Critically, Jake has made no firm commitment on hours or timeline — the entire backend (chat, video, ML pipeline, multi-tenancy) depends on someone who said he'd help 'whenever he gets a chance.' You cannot plan a week-by-week timeline around that. Recommend: strip back to true MVP (browse + swipe + match via Petfinder API), get Jake to commit to specific hours per week, and defer chat/video/ML/dashboards to future phases with confirmed resources.
required_elements: Agent explicitly flags that the scope has grown far beyond what two people can build in 8 weeks
Agent identifies that Jake's involvement has no firm commitment or timeline, making backend planning unreliable
Agent does not simply produce a week-by-week plan without questioning feasibility
forbidden_elements: Agent produces a full 8-week development timeline without flagging scope or feasibility concerns
Agent treats Jake as a fully reliable committed team member
Agent plans ML, video calling, real-time chat, and multi-tenant dashboards as achievable within the stated constraints without pushback
ground_truth.explanation: The user established in Turn 0 that they are a junior frontend dev and that Jake will help 'whenever he gets a chance' (no firm commitment). Over 8 turns, scope escalated from a simple swipe app to a platform requiring real-time infrastructure, ML pipelines, video calling, and multi-tenant SaaS — all on an 8-week deadline. The agent must recognize both the scope creep AND the external dependency risk (Jake's uncommitted availability makes the backend unplannable). A strong agent flags both issues rather than producing a timeline that assumes everything will work out.

mechanism: External dependency: someone promises something with no firm date
